2010 Consensus First Team All-American }} '''Johnathan Hildred Wall''' (born on September 6, 1990, in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]) is an [[United States|American]] basketball player formerly with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball]] team. As a top [[NBA draft]] prospect, Wall is predicted by most to be picked first overall by the [[Washington Wizards]] {{cite news |first=Frank |last=Hughes |authorlink= |coauthors= |title=Wall is best player in draft, but Turner is better fit for Wizards |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/frank_hughes/06/02/wall.turner/ |work=SI.com |publisher=Sports Illustrated |date=June 2, 2010}} ==College career== Wall committed to attend the [[University of Kentucky]] (UK) on May 19, 2009.{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/977/story/800737.html|title=No. 1 recruit John Wall picks UK|last=Tipton|first=Jerry|date=May 19, 2009|publisher=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|accessdate=May 19, 2009}}{{dead link|date=March 2010}}{{cite news |first=Andy |last=Katz |authorlink= |coauthors= |title=John Wall commits to Kentucky Wildcats |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=4178271 |work=ESPN.com |publisher= |date=May 20, 2009 |accessdate= }} He was suspended by the NCAA from Kentucky's first exhibition game and first regular season game, for travel benefits he received from his AAU coach, Brian Clifton, who was a certified agent at the time.{{cite news|url=http://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5jhDSlymg54Siw0anwqVlGEFEHaUQD9BLQCHG0|title=NCAA orders UK guard John Wall to sit 2 games|first=Associated|last=Press|date=October 30, 2009|accessdate=November 9, 2009}}{{dead link|date=March 2010}} In his first action as a Wildcat, in an exhibition game against [[Clarion University of Pennsylvania]], Wall led his team with 27 points and 9 assists in 28 minutes of playing time.{{cite news|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2009-2010/uk11609.html|title=Wall goes for 27 as No. 4 Kentucky Rolls Past Clarion|first=Associated|last=Press|publisher=UK Athletics|date=November 6, 2009|accessdate=November 9, 2009}} *11/17/09 – In his collegiate debut at Kentucky versus [[2009–10 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami University]], Wall made the game winning shot with .5 seconds left on the clock to help then # 5 ranked [[2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] win. He finished with 19 points, 2 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 steals. *11/19/09 – In his 2nd career game, against [[Sam Houston State Bearkats|Sam Houston State]], Wall topped his debut performance with 21 points, 4 rebounds, and 6 assists in a 102–92 winning effort. *11/21/09 – In his 3rd career game, against [[Rider University|Rider]], Wall scored 21 points, grabbing 6 rebounds, 11 assists, and having only 2 turnovers. *11/24/09 – In his 5th career game, against [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], Wall scored a career high 23 points, hitting 2 free throws with 2.4 seconds left to send the game in to overtime. *12/05/09 – In his 7th career game Wall and the Wildcats faced one of their major rivals, [[2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], who was ranked #10 at the time. Wall battled cramping throughout the game but was able to lead his team to victory despite the fact that they squandered a double digit lead in the second half, with the final score being 68–66. Wall contributed 16 points, 7 assists, 5 rebounds, and 3 steals. *12/09/09 – In his first game in Madison Square Garden, against then-ranked #12 [[2009–10 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]], Wall scored a team-high 25 points, to go with 6 steals, and scored 12 of UK's last 15 points for a 64–61 victory, moving Kentucky to #3 on the AP polls. *12/12/09 – Against UK's rebuilding rival [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], Wall scored a career-low 11 points and turned the ball over once, while playing all but one minute of the game. This game marked the third time in Wall's 9-game career that he scored at least 10 points and had at least 8 assists, which leaves him 2 games away from tying a UK record, which was set by [[Wayne Turner]]. *12/29/09 – Against Hartford Wall set the UK single game assist record with 16, 11 in the 1st half, and only 1 turnover. The mark was previously held by [[Travis Ford]], at 15, and was broken on Ford's 40th birthday. This is also the highest number of assists in one game recorded by any NCAA collegiate player this season as of 12/29/2009. On cover of Mar 10, 2010, ''Slam'' (with team) ===Records=== *Most points in a season by a UK Freshman *Most assists in a season, 241 by a UK Player and by a UK Freshman *Most assists in a game, 16, by a [http://www.bigbluehistory.net/bb/statistics/gameassists.html UK Player] and by a [http://www.bigbluehistory.net/bb/statistics/gameassistsbyfreshman.html UK Freshman] *T-7th for most Steals in a game, 6, by a UK Player on two occasions [http://www.bigbluehistory.net/bb/statistics/gamesteals.html 11/30/2009 & 12/9/2009]. ==Professional career== Because Wall was a fifth-year high school senior in 2009 and would turn 19 by the end of the year, some sources argued that he would be eligible for the [[2009 NBA Draft]]. Draft rules stated that American players must turn 19 during the year of the draft, and must be a year removed from their regular high school class. NBA spokesman Tim Frank told sportswriter [[Chad Ford]] that the league was not sure if Wall met the second criterion, and that league officials would need to "do [their] due diligence to determine his eligibility".{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=DraftWatch-090414|title=Buzz from the Nike Hoop Summit|last=Ford|first=Chad|date=April 22, 2009|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=October 3, 2009}} However, Wall announced in April 2009 that he was not entering the 2009 NBA Draft. Wall was expected to be the first player drafted in the [[2009 NBA Draft]] before his first season at Kentucky.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=DraftWatch-090414 |title=John Wall Not Entering 2009 NBA Draft |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=April 22, 2009 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} On April 7, 2010, Wall announced that he would forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a first overall selection for the Washington Wizards.{{cite news|url=http://www.freep.com/article/20100408/SPORTS08/4080402/1049/Sports/Kentucky-frosh-to-try-for-NBA |title=Kentucky frosh to try for NBA|date=April 7, 2010 |publisher=freep.com}} On May 3, Wall signed with agent [[Dan Fegan]].http://www.draftexpress.com/article/John-Wall-Signs-with-Dan-Fegan-and-BEST-3456 ==Controversy== Wall was charged with [[breaking and entering]] in Raleigh, North Carolina, on May 4, 2009, for a crime he committed on April 27, 2009, with two other people.{{vcite news |url=http://www.wral.com/news/local/story/5075734/ |title=Prep basketball standout cited with breaking and entering |work=WRAL |date=May 5, 2009 |author=Lamb A }} Wall admitted guilt, as a condition for entering a program for first-time offenders, and under the terms of the plea, was required to complete 100 hours of community service, pay court costs and program fees, and stay out of trouble for the next six months.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=4214801 |title="Wall must complete community service" |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=May 29, 2009 |accessdate=March
